hero.headline: Conversation is part of the project.

bio.p1: I'm a freelance web developer based in Chianti, between Siena and Florence, working with businesses across Tuscany and Italy. I help restaurants, farm stays, B&Bs and small businesses build an online presence that actually works.
bio.p2: My job isn't just writing code — it's understanding your needs, turning them into a concrete plan and seeing it through with you all the way. Every site I build is designed to be fast, easy to find on Google and simple to manage.
bio.p3: I work with modern technologies like React, Next.js, WordPress and Tailwind CSS. But technology is just a tool: what matters is the results it brings to your business.

ecommerce.problem: You want to sell online but don't know how

workflow.title: How I <highlight>work</highlight>
workflow.text: From first contact to post-launch support, every stage is transparent.

contact.title: First contact
contact.description: We get to know each other over a call or a coffee. You tell me about your business, your goals and your needs. I listen and take notes.

analysis.title: Analysis and proposal
analysis.description: I study your industry, your competitors and the opportunities. Then I present a clear proposal with defined timelines, costs and deliverables.

design.title: Design and prototypes
design.description: I create wireframes and mockups of the site. We review them together and iterate until you're happy, before a single line of code is written.

development.title: Development
development.description: I build the site with the agreed technologies. I keep you posted with regular previews and gather your feedback along the way.

launch.title: Launch
launch.description: Final testing, performance and SEO optimization, hosting and domain setup. The site goes live and I show you how to manage it on your own.

support.title: Post-launch support
support.description: I don't disappear after delivery. I'm still around for updates, fixes and improvements. Your site grows with your business.

items.q: How much does a website cost?
items.a: It depends on the complexity of the project. A business website starts at around €1,000; an online store or a project with custom features can cost more. I always give you a clear, detailed quote before we start.
A business website takes 2–4 weeks on average. More complex projects like online stores or web applications can take 4–6 weeks. Timelines also depend on how quickly I receive content and feedback.

items.q: Do you only work with businesses in Chianti?
items.a: No, I work with clients all over Italy, remotely too. In the Siena and Florence areas I can also meet you in person. Chianti is my home, and for local businesses I can offer something extra: I know the area, the audience and how things work here.

items.q: Can I update the site myself after delivery?
items.a: Absolutely. If the project calls for it, I use WordPress as a CMS so you can manage content, images and text on your own. I also give you a short training session so you can get started with confidence.
I don't disappear. I offer post-launch support for fixes, updates and optimizations. We can also agree on a monthly maintenance plan if you'd like ongoing assistance.
Every site I build comes with solid SEO foundations: semantic structure, speed, meta tags, sitemap. For advanced SEO strategies and ranking campaigns, we can discuss a dedicated plan.
Mainly React, Next.js, TypeScript, MaterialUI and WordPress (headless too). The choice depends on the project — I always use the right tool for the job, not the trendiest one.
Yes, I always work with a written, accepted quote that defines scope, timeline, costs and payment terms. Clarity from the start, for both of us.

hero.title: Recent <highlight>work</highlight>
hero.text: Every project tells a different story. Here are the ones I'm working on and the ones already live.

radici.subtitle: Non-profit community association
radici.description: Website for an association that promotes the Chianti and Gaiole area. Event management, a network of local partners, and hiking trails with GPX tracks and elevation profiles. The main challenge: a custom interactive map with Leaflet, dynamic clustering, category filters and a smooth UX on every device.
features: Custom Post Types (events, partners, excursions, trails)

succulentarte.subtitle: Renzo Vannetti — Succulent plant artistry
succulentarte.description: Showcase website for my father Renzo's business, creating artistic arrangements with succulent plants. A clean design that puts his creations front and center, with a photo gallery and contact details.

casanova.subtitle: Wine estate — Gaiole in Chianti
casanova.description: Website for a winery in the heart of Chianti Classico. It tells the story of the Rossi family, their land, the beekeeping project and the tastings and farm-stay offering. Bilingual Italian/English.

cresta.subtitle: Trekking route along the Chianti ridge
cresta.description: Website dedicated to the Michaelic pilgrimage route along the ridge of the Chianti Mountains: 70 km from Castelnuovo Berardenga to Strada in Chianti. Route map, stages, history and practical information for hikers.

cantinetta.subtitle: Wine shop in Gaiole in Chianti — Since 2003
cantinetta.description: Showcase website for a historic wine shop in the heart of Chianti Classico. Headless architecture with WordPress as the CMS and Next.js on the frontend. An elegant design system with a merlot red palette, a photo gallery with albums, and wine and local-product pages with dynamic filters.

glam.subtitle: Weddings & Events — Tuscany
glam.description: SEO consulting and GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) for a wedding and events agency in Tuscany. Work on content structure, schema markup and visibility in AI-assisted search.
glam.label: SEO/GEO only

tecnochianti.subtitle: Architecture & engineering firm — Radda in Chianti
tecnochianti.description: Portfolio website for a technical firm bringing together three professionals in architecture and building services. A "typographic architecture" direction: large serif headlines, images front and center on a light background and a near-monochrome palette with a terracotta accent. Project previews fade from black and white to color on hover.
